title: Documentation Enhancement: Remove redundancy in build instructions.
description:
I wanted to get started building Wireshark so that I could contribute.  These instructions were the most prominent place I landed:

https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsug_html_chunked/ChBuildInstallUnixBuild.html

However, they didn't help me get started very quickly.  Most notably, I was unable to find a list of dependencies.

Later, I found that there were at least 3 different build instructions among the documents.  I've consolidated all to one place, paying attention not to lose anything.

I've replaced the redundant instructions with links to the one place (obviously, this is not yet updated):

https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsdg_html_chunked/ChapterSetup.html

Summary of changes made:

* Consolidate build instructions and troubleshooting into WSDG chapter 2.

* Link from WSUG build instructions to the WSDG chapters.

* Reorder WSUG to have install instructions before build instructions for both
Windows and Unix.

* Link from WSDG build instructions in WSDG sources chapter back to
WSDG chapter 2.

* Add --depth=100 option to git clone command lines in obtaining sources.

Is this true?  We define HAVE_LIBPCAP and I think there have been MRs to fix building without libpcap.

Yes, we support building without pcap.

It does *not* appear to be a required package; we find it with

    ws_find_package(PCAP ENABLE_PCAP HAVE_LIBPCAP)

`ws_find_package()` does not pass `REQUIRED` to `find_package()`.

(Furthermore, if the Boolean variable whose name is the second argument to `ws_find_package()` is not true, it doesn't even bother to call `find_package()` to find the package, as that's an indication that you don't want to build with that package.

In this case, if you don't have pcap, but don't turn `ENABLE_PCAP` off, it'll try to find it, note that it didn't, but it should just drive on with `HAVE_LIBPCAP` not defined to be true.)

`--depth=100` will cause issues with packaging and anything else that depends on `git describe` when we accumulate more than 100 commits since the most recent tag (v3.5.1rc0) in the next week or so. There are typically a lot of commits between a major release branch fork and the next development release:

```
$ git describe v3.5.0~1
v3.5.0rc0-2825-gb7ff41703e
$ git describe v3.3.0~1
v3.3.0rc0-2054-g3426b25621
$ git describe v3.1.0~1
v3.1.0rc0-1391-g76e227bcef
```

We use `--depth=5000` in `.gitlab-ci.yml`, but that's more due to git lacking a `clone --shallow-include='v*'` and GitLab's limited ability to customize cloning more than a fondness for `--depth=`.

I agree with @alagoutte that a note or comment might be better, e.g.

```
# If you have a GitLab account, you can use the SSH URL:
$ git clone -o upstream git@gitlab.com:wireshark/wireshark.git
# If you don't you can use the HTTPS URL:
$ git clone -o upstream https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark.git
# You can speed up cloning in either case by adding --shallow-since=1year or --depth=5000.
```
